transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. From what you have described, the most likely cause is sump / tub-to-pump hose. Next: Establish WHERE the water appears, WHEN in the cycle, and what it LOOKS like before choosing a part. Let me know what you find.

I'm standing in my socks on the wet floor right now, should I get out of it?? The fuse box is in the hall and the floor there is dry so I can turn it off from there. Should I do that first before looking at where the water's coming from?

Yes, step off the wet floor now and don't touch the machine, the plug or the socket while water is near them. Since the floor by your fuse box is dry, switch off the washing machine's circuit there (or the main switch if you're not sure which one it is) before you go back to look at the water. Is the leaking water clean, soapy/dirty wash water, or dirty/oily-looking water?
ok I'm going to the hall now to switch it off. The water just looks like normal wash water I think, no foam. Is it ok to go back and look once the power's off?

Yes, once the power is off at the fuse box in the hall (where the floor is dry), not by touching the plug or socket in the wet area, it's safe to go back and look. Put some shoes on and mop up the standing water before you get down to the machine. Next: If it started after cleaning the filter, re-seat the filter cap/seal and check the sealing face before suspecting the pump. Let me know what you find.
ok the power's off at the fuse box and I've put shoes on. I haven't cleaned any filter or anything. The water seems to be mostly at the front under the door. What should I check next?

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the pump filter cap or its seal. The pump filter cap at the bottom front is a common leak, especially if it's been opened recently. Check it's screwed in fully and straight, and that its rubber seal is clean. Was it loose or not seated, tight and dry already, or is the cap or seal cracked or damaged?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I checked the filter cap at the bottom, it's tight and the area behind the flap is dry. I also had a look at the rubber door seal and there's a small split in the bottom fold, with an underwire from a bra stuck next to it. Is that the cause?

Yes, that split is the most likely cause. A split in the bottom fold of the door seal typically leaks wash water at the front under the door, and a trapped underwire is a common culprit. From what you have described, the most likely cause is the rubber door seal. Check the grey drain hose along its length and where it goes into the standpipe or sink waste. Was it loose or pushed in too far, sound and dry, or is the hose split or cracked?

I can't pull the machine out on my own, it's full of water and really heavy, so I can't see along the drain hose. The split in the seal is the only thing I've found. Is that enough to go on, and is it safe to use the machine again?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, a split in the bottom fold of the door seal fits a leak of plain wash water at the front under the door, so it's enough to go on. The machine isn't safe to use again until the seal is replaced, and because water has reached the plug, don't touch the plug or the machine while you're in wet socks: put dry shoes on and switch the washing machine's circuit off at the fuse box, where the floor is The checks point to the door seal. To find the right part, could you give me the model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok, I've found the label and the model number is WTK72041W. Is that what you need?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, the split in the bottom fold of the door seal, likely caused by the bra underwire, is enough to explain water collecting at the front under the door. Because the machine is still running and water has reached the plug, do not touch the machine or plug while standing on the wet floor in socks. The checks point to the door seal.
